title: Convoso & Call Conduct
summary: Use the Convoso dialer the right way and stay clear of call avoidance and improper call handling.

blocks.html:
• Convoso only runs in Google Chrome.
  • Copy the Convoso link from your team channel and log in.
  • Allow the microphone. Pick "Allow while visiting the site."
  • Select the Medicare calling campaign you're assigned and set your status.

Statuses:

  • Available: you're taking calls.
  • Break: 5 minutes or less, and not during power hours.
  • Training: only when a manager pulls you.
  • Personal Callback: for your scheduled callbacks.
  • Lunch: 1:00 to 2:00 PM only.
  • Logout: end of shift.

blocks.title: NEVER use Not Ready
blocks.html: There is a Not Ready status. Never use it.

blocks.question: Which browser does Convoso run in?
blocks.explanation: Convoso only runs in Google Chrome.

blocks.question: Which status should you NEVER use?

blocks.html:
• Transfer: press the transfer button.
  • Red X: the red X next to a line disconnects that line. Use it to drop a failed agent attempt, then press transfer again.
  • Leave Conference Call: press it once you've heard both parties speak, then disposition as Transfer.
  • Lead hangs up: you get a pop-up. Click wrap-up and disposition.
  • Pausing after a call: pick the status from the dropdown before you disposition.
  • Editing customer info: Contact tab, scroll down, Apply Changes. Click the Script tab to go back.

blocks.title: Failed attempt? Red X, then transfer
blocks.html: If an agent attempt fails, don't hang up on the consumer. Use the red X next to the agent's line only, then press transfer again.

blocks.question: An agent attempt fails. How do you drop just that line?
choices: Click the red X next to that line, then press transfer again
Set your status to Not Ready
blocks.explanation: The red X disconnects a single line.

blocks.question: You need to take a break after this call. When do you pick the status?
choices: From the dropdown before you disposition
You can't pause after a call
blocks.explanation: Pick the status from the dropdown before dispositioning.

blocks.question: How do you update a consumer's contact info?
choices: Contact tab, scroll down, Apply Changes, then click the Script tab to return
Ask the specialist to do it
blocks.explanation: Edit in the Contact tab and Apply Changes.

blocks.html:
Setting a callback: the Callback disposition needs a time.

  1. Click the blank space next to time.
  2. Pick the date, hour and time.
  3. Set the type to Personal Callback.
  4. Disposition as Callback.

Making a scheduled callback:

  1. Set your status to Personal Callback.
  2. Go to the History tab.
  3. Select the call.
  4. Click the green phone icon in the primary phone field.

blocks.title: Remember the 15 minutes
blocks.html: Every scheduled callback must be at least 15 minutes out.

blocks.question: How do you place a scheduled callback?
choices: Set Not Ready and dial manually
Set Personal Callback status, go to History, select the call, click the green phone icon
Set Available status and wait for the dialer
blocks.explanation: Personal Callback status, History tab, select the call, green phone icon.

blocks.question: What callback type do you choose when scheduling?
blocks.explanation: Set the type to Personal Callback, then disposition as Callback.

lessons.title: Zero Tolerance: Call Avoidance & Improper Handling

blocks.html:
These are zero tolerance. Don't do them.

Call avoidance:

  • Staying in wrap-up or unavailable without approval
  • Not greeting the lead within a reasonable time
  • Hanging up when leads connect, or cherry-picking calls
  • Extending call time unnecessarily
  • Staying on dead calls or answering machines too long
  • Failing to rebut when the lead objects
  • Failing to rebut separate objections
  • Anything meant to delay or avoid calls

Improper call handling:

  • Profanity or inappropriate language
  • Being rude or unprofessional (volume, tone, word choice)
  • Patterns of miscoding, mishandling transfers, or no agents
  • Failing to follow compliance guidelines

blocks.title: Zero tolerance means zero
blocks.html: These aren't small mistakes. They can cost you your seat. Stay Available, greet fast, rebut every objection, code accurately.

blocks.question: A lead connects and you hang up because they "sounded old and slow." What is this?
choices: Call avoidance (hanging up when leads connect / cherry-picking)
Allowed if you're behind on transfers
blocks.explanation: Hanging up on connected leads or cherry-picking is call avoidance.

blocks.question: Which of these is improper call handling?
choices: Raising your voice at a consumer
blocks.explanation: Being rude or unprofessional in volume, tone, or word choice is improper call handling.

questions.question: What do you click when Chrome asks about the microphone?
questions.explanation: Allow the microphone: "Allow while visiting the site."

questions.question: How long can a Break status last?
choices: 5 minutes or less, not during power hours
questions.explanation: Break is 5 minutes or less and not in power hours.

questions.question: When is the Training status used?
choices: Whenever you want to review the script
Only when a manager pulls you
questions.explanation: Training is only when a manager pulls you.

questions.question: A lead hangs up and you get a pop-up. What do you do?
choices: Wait for the next call without coding

questions.question: What do you press after hearing both parties speak on a transfer?
choices: The red X on the consumer's line
questions.explanation: Leave Conference Call, then disposition as Transfer.

questions.question: Which is call avoidance?
questions.explanation: Staying in wrap-up or unavailable without approval is call avoidance.

questions.question: Which is call avoidance?
choices: Leaving the conference after both parties speak
Using Personal Callback for a scheduled callback
Staying on an answering machine too long
questions.explanation: Staying on dead calls or answering machines too long is call avoidance.

questions.question: A consumer objects and you just say "okay, bye" without a rebuttal. What is this?
questions.explanation: Failing to rebut when the lead objects is call avoidance.

questions.question: Which status do you use at the end of your shift?
questions.explanation: Logout at the end of shift. Never Not Ready.

questions.question: What is on the improper call handling list?
choices: Patterns of miscoding, mishandling transfers or no agents
Using the red X on a failed agent line
questions.explanation: Patterns of miscoding are improper call handling.
